title: fix(update): keep valid cold archives from blocking updates
body:
Fixes #200594

## What Problem This Solves

An update from 2026.11.4 to the 2026.11.5 candidate can roll back because rehearsal Doctor reports an intact cold transcript archive as missing. The copied agent database keeps its file-backed archive rows, but the snapshot omits their payloads.

## User Impact

Rehearsal now preserves the live representation: `storage='file'`, a null blob, and payload files at the copied store's resolved cold path. Missing referenced files stop capture; corrupt payloads retain the normal read-verification failure. No schema, config, or updater protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot producer projects the files referenced by the copied rows, including chunk files. Regular immutable files use hard links; unsupported or cross-filesystem links fall back to a reflink or exclusive byte copy. Symlinks receive independent copies. The source database and archive bytes remain unchanged.

Link safety follows the existing cold writer: [`session-accessor.sqlite-archive-artifact.ts:203–225`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-artifact.ts#L203) verifies and reuses an existing file, or publishes a new inode exclusively. It never overwrites an existing cold payload. Reset only unlinks its selected name ([`session-accessor.sqlite-reset.ts:193`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reset.ts#L193)). The projector does not chmod shared inodes.

Inventory measures referenced payload sizes through a metadata-only read snapshot. Those bytes enter the historical `pluginBytes` wire allowance ([`update-candidate-state.ts:235`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b/src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts#L235)), which released parents already include in their free-space and I/O-time estimates. This reserves the full copy fallback even when linking is cheap, excludes orphans, and avoids decoding payloads or embedding them into SQLite.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and Doctor read set</summary>

The defect was verified on main `235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649`: [`update-candidate-state.ts:630–717`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649/src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts#L630) copied database rows but transformed only shared state. No agent cold-file copy ran. All external payloads were omitted; there was no selective size, age, mode, or count filter. The reader resolves them under the copied store's sibling `sessions/cold/` directory.

The reported candidate revision `e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` has no cold-navigation migration. That newer-main path does not identify this historical failure.

- Candidate Doctor invokes legacy-main migration, then canonical-key repair ([`doctor-session-transcripts.ts:237–250`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.ts#L237)).
- Legacy-main repair restores cold claims when source and destination physical stores or cold directories differ ([`legacy-main-session-migration.ts:584–597`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/src/config/sessions/legacy-main-session-migration.ts#L584)).
- Canonical repair skips unaffected groups. It selects duplicate, raw-comparison, lineage, key-normalization, or physical-owner repairs ([`doctor-session-canonical-candidates.ts:241–251`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/src/commands/doctor-session-canonical-candidates.ts#L241)), then restores only the selected keys' referenced generations ([`session-accessor.sqlite-canonical-repair.ts:117–143`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-canonical-repair.ts#L117)). Its awaited restore loop propagates the first failure, so one reported filename does not establish that only one payload was absent or would be read. These reads protect history before copying or archiving it.

</details>

## Evidence

- Real SQLite, real compressed files, and the candidate snapshot subprocess preserve file-backed rows and null blobs. Restoration after the whole source state directory becomes unavailable reproduces the original ENOENT failure on task base `57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f` and passes with this fix. Live missing/corrupt diagnostics remain asserted; a corrupt rehearsal file also fails normal verification.
- Against rejected review head `0d3fa05646d8a37c22d1c68c2dfaa67fa6768bc1`, the four-case regression file had **3 failures / 1 pass**, exposing changed row shape, eager corruption handling, and omitted capacity bytes. With the revision, all four pass.
- **51 tests passed at accepted design head `f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b`** in the four named suites: `update-candidate-state.cold-archives.test.ts` (4), `update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts` (19), `session-cold-storage.test.ts` (21), and `session-cold-storage.chunks.test.ts` (7). The chunk projection test forces EXDEV for one link, proves a distinct fallback inode, removes source files, and decodes exact copied events. The single-file regression proves actual hard-link identity. The real parent capacity assertion includes the exact payload bytes.
- Command: `pnpm test src/infra/update-candidate-state.cold-archives.test.ts src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.chunks.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Wall time **117.87s**, including cold compilation. The four regression cases execute in 17.66s; the new chunk/fallback case takes 42ms. These are prior-head results; current repair results follow below.
- Exact CI core-leaf type-aware/type-checking oxlint passes for all four touched TypeScript files. Touched-file oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.
- Pr-simplify complete: removed snapshot embedding; one file-selection owner serves sizing and projection. Against task base: +115 production lines, +196 test lines, +15 documentation lines. The CI repair adds no helper or fallback; it removes the closed-WAL opt-in, names the existing worker boundary, and strengthens the existing regression. Growth implements file projection and compatible capacity accounting, with no new durable state or manager.
- Independent delta autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete five-file local change against `0d3fa05646d8a37c22d1c68c2dfaa67fa6768bc1`: **scoped-clean, no findings**. That review covered the accepted design revision; the CI-repair delta has its own review below.


- CI repair: the SQL helper already runs exclusively through the candidate-state subprocess's inventory and snapshot operations ([`update-candidate-state.worker.ts:146`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3423beb43d050b09136c4f786efe34234fd0c73c/src/infra/update-candidate-state.worker.ts#L146), [line 169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3423beb43d050b09136c4f786efe34234fd0c73c/src/infra/update-candidate-state.worker.ts#L169)). Renaming it to `update-candidate-cold-archives.worker.ts` gives the database-worker inventory the documented worker classification. No baseline or allowance changed.
- The header-cleanup CI failure came from inventory's `allowClosedWal: true` read creating WAL/SHM files on a closed WAL source. The later header inspection consequently took a direct read and never created the private header copy whose failed cleanup it should retain. Removing that opt-in ([`update-candidate-cold-archives.worker.ts:68`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3423beb43d050b09136c4f786efe34234fd0c73c/src/infra/update-candidate-cold-archives.worker.ts#L68)) uses the existing private-copy fallback and preserves the source family. The original assertion is unchanged. It reproduced **1 failure / 3 passes** on `f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b`; stronger post-inventory sidecar checks reproduced **4 failures / 0 passes** before the production fix.
- Current repair: **34 tests pass**, in `update-candidate-state.header-cleanup.test.ts` (4), `update-candidate-state.cold-archives.test.ts` (4), `update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts` (19), and `session-cold-storage.chunks.test.ts` (7), in one named-file run with `--maxWorkers=1` (**79.99s**, including compilation). These cover retained cleanup custody, source preservation, file-backed row fidelity, missing/corrupt archives, fallback projection, and capacity accounting.
- CI-core typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass on the repair's four touched TypeScript files. The single named database-worker ratchet script passes against task base `57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f`: **T1 166 → 166; T1-compat 15 → 15**, with no baseline or allowance edits (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-worker-ratchet.mts --base 57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f --no-merge-base`).
- Independent delta autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), base `f40dedc91a81ea1afd28ff43de15813dfae90f2b` through the staged four-file repair now committed as `3423beb43d050b09136c4f786efe34234fd0c73c`: **scoped-clean, no findings**. No reviewed source changed afterward.

Limits: the saved report and live issue comments do not identify the affected session key or failing Doctor phase, so the exact predicate selecting the reporter's row remains unconfirmed. No full macOS published 11.4 → candidate update or package build was run; the configured Crabbox provider refused the named-suite request because its API key is missing. SQLite is qualified here; PostgreSQL export paths were not exercised. Files created after inventory retain the existing live-growth limit of the estimate. Broad proof is left to PR CI.

Reported by @SimonAIbot (with detailed archive evidence)
